chunks: And it was narrated from Ḥarīz ibn ʿAbdillāh that he said:
I was with Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and a man asked him. He said to him, “May I be sacrificed for you, indeed the sun descends, then becomes still for a moment before it declines.”
So he said: “It consults whether it should decline or not decline.”

key_terms.الشَّمْسَ: the sun, as the celestial body being discussed
key_terms.تَنْقَضُّ: appears to descend or move downward
key_terms.تُؤَامِرُ: consults or is caused to deliberate
key_terms.سَاعَةً: for a short while or moment

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام say about the sun pausing before noon?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a question posed to Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام about the apparent pause of the sun before its decline. The Imam عليه السلام answers with a cosmological expression indicating that the sun is under divine order and determination.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.677 - It was narrated from Hariz ibn Abdullah that He said:

I was with Abu 'Abdillah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) when a man asked him,
"May I be sacrificed for you, the sun seems to descend (move downward) and then becomes still for a moment before it reaches its zenith."
Imam (as) replied: "It consults whether it should continue or not”.
